parents.name: Reading First's decoding gains justify treating the program as an educational success.
parents.description: This evaluative position gives substantial weight to improved first-grade decoding despite no statistically significant comprehension gains in grades 1–3. The evaluation supplies the findings; it does not establish this judgment of overall success.

parents.name: Reading First should not be judged successful without demonstrated gains in reading comprehension.
parents.description: This evaluative position treats demonstrated comprehension gains as necessary for program success. It acknowledges the measured first-grade decoding improvement while disputing whether that benefit is sufficient.

pairs.reason: These explicitly disagree over whether decoding gains are sufficient for a success judgment when comprehension gains are not demonstrated. Both are evaluative, not attributed report conclusions.
